hints: Which quantities depend only on the vertical motion? The wind changes only the horizontal motion, from uniform to uniformly accelerated.
worded:
1. H = 45 m gives u_y = √(2 × 10 × 45) = 30 m/s and a time of flight of 6 s.

2. R = 90 m in 6 s gives u_x = 15 m/s.

3. The wind adds a horizontal acceleration only. Time of flight and maximum height depend only on the vertical motion, so they stay 6 s and 45 m.

4. New range = u_xT + ½aT² = 90 + ½ × 1 × 36 = 108 m. (C)

5. Check: (A) and (B) add only 9 m (half the extra), and (B) wrongly changes H.
conventional:
![](asset:P000218-sol-1)

$$H = \frac{u_{y}^{2}}{2g} = 45 \Rightarrow u_{y} = 30\unit{m/s},\quad T = \frac{2u_{y}}{g} = 6\unit{s},\quad u_{x} = \frac{90}{6} = 15\unit{m/s}.$$

With $a_{x} = g/10 = 1$ m/s²:

$$R\prime = u_{x}T + \frac{1}{2}a_{x}T^{2} = 90 + \frac{1}{2}(1)(36) = 108\unit{m},\quad\quad H\prime = H = 45\unit{m}.$$
mistakes: A horizontal wind does not change the height or the time of flight.
Add ½aT², not ½aT² with T = 3 s (the time to the top).
